00387.title: Cisplatin every 3 weeks + head and neck radiotherapy
00387.setting: Locally advanced stage III–IV squamous head and neck cancer.
00387.purpose: Cisplatin and radiotherapy work together to treat locally advanced head and neck cancer. Your team explains the treatment aim, likely benefit and alternatives for your diagnosis.
00387.schedule: Cisplatin 100 mg/m² on Day 1 every 21 days for three planned cycles during radiotherapy. Cisplatin is given before radiation on the same day. If radiotherapy is cancelled, cisplatin is held until radiation resumes; the team updates both calendars.

risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Hearing loss or tinnitus, which can persist
Infusion reaction and effects on fertility
Dry mouth, taste and saliva changes
Skin reaction in the treated area
Some swallowing, saliva or tissue effects can be lasting

00387.discussion: Discuss the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty; serious or lasting harms; treatment burden; fertility and pregnancy precautions; and the patient’s priorities. Explain blood-count suppression/infection, nausea, kidney/mineral injury, hearing loss and neuropathy that can persist, hydration and same-day radiation coordination. Discuss radiation mouth, skin, swallowing, saliva, dental and jaw effects, including lasting effects and potential nutritional support. Radiation has its own consent process. Confirm actual urgent contacts and teach-back; this draft does not authorise treatment.
limitations: Cisplatin dose, treatment setting and cancer site affect applicability.
No survival figure from a different regimen or disease is presented as the benefit of this treatment.
support: Ask for one schedule showing prevention medicines, rescue treatment and what to do if symptoms persist. Do not add, double or restart medicines from an old prescription.

Cisplatin needs prescribed fluids before and after infusion. Follow the team’s drinking advice and report much less urine, vomiting or inability to drink. Do not change fluid intake or diuretics without advice.

A dietitian can tailor food texture, supplements and calorie or protein needs. Tell the team early if eating or drinking becomes difficult; do not wait for substantial weight loss. Fluid targets depend on kidney and heart health.

Use the mouth-care plan provided by the team and tell them about ulcers, thrush, bleeding or pain. Inform your dentist about cancer treatment. Before any dental procedure, confirm timing with the oncology team.

A speech and language therapist can assess swallowing and advise exercises or safer food and drink textures. Follow the individual assessment; a general guide cannot decide which textures are safe for you.

Discuss fertility and pregnancy precautions before treatment and the medicine-specific duration of contraception afterwards. Ask about breastfeeding. Bring a full medicine, supplement and allergy list; check before adding over-the-counter or herbal products.
00387.review_status: Source reconciled draft; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

00207/head_neck.title: Weekly cetuximab + head and neck radiotherapy
00207/head_neck.setting: Locally advanced squamous head and neck cancer in people ineligible for platinum-based treatment.
00207/head_neck.purpose: Cetuximab is combined with radiotherapy for selected locally advanced head and neck cancer when platinum chemotherapy is unsuitable. The team discusses the reason for choosing this treatment and the alternatives.
00207/head_neck.schedule: Cetuximab starts one week before radiotherapy: a 400 mg/m² first infusion, then 250 mg/m² every week during radiation until radiotherapy ends. The number of weekly doses follows the actual radiotherapy plan.

risks: Acne-like rash, dry skin and nail infection
Low magnesium and other mineral changes
Dry mouth, taste and saliva changes
Skin reaction in the treated area
Some swallowing, saliva or tissue effects can be lasting

00207/head_neck.discussion: Discuss the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty; serious or lasting harms; treatment burden; fertility and pregnancy precautions; and the patient’s priorities. Explain infusion anaphylaxis, rash and nail/eye problems, mineral loss and post-treatment testing; the observation plan requires reconciliation of NCCP and product information. Discuss radiation mouth, skin, swallowing, saliva, dental and jaw effects, including lasting effects and potential nutritional support. Radiation has its own consent process. Confirm actual urgent contacts and teach-back; this draft does not authorise treatment.
limitations: Apply current NCCP platinum-ineligible selection; trial enrolment and present-day selection are different.
Do not import colorectal cetuximab evidence, RAS criteria or metastatic survival figures into this radiation pathway.
support: Ask for one schedule showing prevention medicines, rescue treatment and what to do if symptoms persist. Do not add, double or restart medicines from an old prescription.

00705.title: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin + fluorouracil
00705.setting: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in adults with tumour PD-L1 CPS ≥1.
00705.purpose: Pembrolizumab and chemotherapy aim to control head and neck cancer that has spread or returned and cannot be removed. Your team explains the expected benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for you.
00705.schedule: Every 21 days: pembrolizumab and carboplatin on Day 1; fluorouracil over Days 1–4. Up to 6 combination cycles, then pembrolizumab alone while appropriate. Every dose depends on safety and benefit review.

risks: Immune inflammation of bowel, lungs, liver or kidneys
Thyroid, pituitary, adrenal or glucose problems
Rare heart, muscle, nerve and eye inflammation
Some immune effects need long-term treatment
Low blood counts and serious infection
Low blood counts and serious infection
Rare severe neurological or early excessive toxicity

00705.discussion: Discuss the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty; serious or lasting harms; treatment burden; fertility and pregnancy precautions; and the patient’s priorities. Explain low blood counts/infection, bleeding, nausea, mucositis, diarrhoea, fluorouracil cardiac and early severe toxicity, platinum kidney/hearing/nerve effects, DPD testing limits, pump/line complications and immune organ inflammation including permanent hormone replacement. Separate the up-to-six-cycle combination phase from ongoing pembrolizumab maintenance. Confirm actual urgent contacts and teach-back; this draft does not authorise treatment.
limitations: The current NCCP indication requires PD-L1 CPS ≥1; a trial’s total population is not a replacement eligibility rule.
The trial was not a direct comparison of carboplatin with cisplatin.
Trial treatment duration does not impose an automatic duration cap absent from the current NCCP regimen.
Group outcomes do not predict an individual outcome.
support: Ask for one schedule showing prevention medicines, rescue treatment and what to do if symptoms persist. Do not add, double or restart medicines from an old prescription.

Pembrolizumab can cause inflammation in healthy organs even after chemotherapy has finished. Keep the alert card and report new symptoms promptly. Steroids or hormone replacement may be needed for specific complications; do not start or stop them without the treating team.

A dietitian can tailor food texture, supplements and calorie or protein needs. Tell the team early if eating or drinking becomes difficult; do not wait for substantial weight loss. Fluid targets depend on kidney and heart health.

Use the mouth-care plan provided by the team and tell them about ulcers, thrush, bleeding or pain. Inform your dentist about cancer treatment. Before any dental procedure, confirm timing with the oncology team.

A speech and language therapist can assess swallowing and advise exercises or safer food and drink textures. Follow the individual assessment; a general guide cannot decide which textures are safe for you.

Discuss fertility and pregnancy precautions before treatment and the medicine-specific duration of contraception afterwards. Ask about breastfeeding. Bring a full medicine, supplement and allergy list; check before adding over-the-counter or herbal products.
